battle.name: 成都之戰
battle.brief: 咸通十年十月，南詔驃信世隆領兵攻成都，先破董春烏部，再連下犍為、嘉州，焚掠陵州、榮州與黎雅二州，次年正月兵抵成都城下。唐軍固守子城，新募三千突將出城反擊，援軍合戰於新都、星宿山，南詔始退。卡面的埃及長矛，正是守城步兵所用的長柄兵器，與弓弩、火油、雲梯同現於成都城頭。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 咸通十年十月開戰的兩方，是唐與南詔。唐方的戰線沿成都周邊與大渡河上游展開：西川節度使盧耽總攏成都城防，東川節度使竇滂領定邊軍屯於黎雅一線，忠武軍、徐宿軍、兗海軍分屯大渡河兩岸，節度使、觀察使之下設都頭、監軍、游弈使各分部眾；調兵則由朝廷下詔，先後徵發興元府六千人、鳳翔府四千人在漢州集結待命，又有左神武將軍顏慶復、右武衛上將軍宋威各率本軍星夜入蜀。南詔方面以驃信世隆為最高統帥，親領主力自雲南沿山谷北進，其下有清平官與諸部將領分領兵眾，能在一日之內拆出數路奇兵，並在攻城屢遣使議和，以行緩兵之計。唐方出兵的序列並不單一：既有節度使直轄的城防兵與臨時募兵，也有京畿宿衛調來的諸道軍，另有州刺史與縣令組織的團練鄉兵，彼此指揮鏈條鬆散，多賴臨陣商議與詔令協調；被貶的東川節度使竇滂甚至能以一句敵眾數十倍之說，使興元、鳳翔兩路援軍在漢州觀望不進，這說明此時節度使之間的隸屬關係仍靠朝廷詔書維持，尚未有唐末五代那種割據式的獨立指揮體系。
countriesEn: The two parties that went to war in the tenth month of Xiantong were the Tang and Nanzhao. The Tang front ran along the approaches to Chengdu and the upper reaches of the Dadu river: the Xichuan military governor Lu Dan took charge of the defence of the city itself, the Dongchuan military governor Dou Pang led the Dingbian army in the Li-Ya line, and the Zhongwu, Xusu and Yuanhai armies were posted on both banks of the Dadu; below the governors and the inspecting commissioners stood army heads, commissaries and patrol officers, each with his own detachment. Troops were moved by imperial orders, and the court first summoned six thousand men from Xingyuan Prefecture and four thousand from Fengxiang Prefecture to assemble at Hanzhou and wait, while the Left Shenwu general Yan Qingfu and the Right Wuwei general Song Wei each led their own command into Sichuan by forced night marches. On the Nanzhao side the supreme commander was the chieftain Shilang, who led the main body north from Yunnan through the mountain valleys, with his civil administrators and the commanders of the various tribal contingents holding separate troops; he could split off several columns of surprise troops within a single day, and in front of the walls he repeatedly sent envoys to talk, in order to slow the Tang army down. The Tang force was by no means a single chain of command: there were the city garrison and the hastily recruited men under the governor's own hand, the commands of several circuits transferred out of the capital region, and the militia bands organised by prefects and county magistrates; the chain of command between them was loose and had to be held together by conference on the spot and by the wording of imperial orders. Dou Pang, the governor who was later demoted, could even stop the reinforcements from Xingyuan and Fengxiang in their tracks at Hanzhou with a single claim that the enemy was ten times their number, which shows that the subordination of the governors was still maintained by the wording of the court's decrees and had not yet hardened into the independent command systems of the late Tang and the Five Dynasties.
people: 此役最先被記下來的名字是定邊節度使李師望：咸通十年，他為求邊功，殺死南詔使者楊酋慶，把一場本可通好的糾紛變成開戰的理由；朝廷隨後以太府少卿竇滂代之，竇滂到任便失清溪關、失犍為、失嘉州，在大渡河邊的交鋒中驚恐投環自縊，被徐州將領苗全緒救下，隨後單騎逃奔導江，事後貶為康州司戶。守土有功者是定邊軍都頭安再榮，他退守大渡河北岸，與南詔隔水互射，堅持九天八夜；兗海將領黃卓奉命率五百人赴沐源川阻擊，全軍覆沒，沒有回報。成都方面的樞紐是節度使盧耽，他急召彭州刺史吳行魯與前瀘州刺史楊慶復共修守備，張榜招募勇士三千，編為「突將」。楊慶復與攝左都押牙李驤各率突將出城，殺傷攻城之敵二千餘人、焚燒敵方攻具三千餘具，又以熔化鐵汁從城上澆下，擊退以濕篷蔽身的敵軍。先鋒游弈使王晝奉命赴漢州求援，太僕卿支詳奉詔為宣諭通和使，南詔則遣清平官楊定保議和；右武衛上將軍宋威率忠武軍二千人趕到，與諸軍合戰，終使南詔退保星宿山。城內還有人暗中通敵，防守大將李自孝私與南詔相約，準備焚燒東倉作內應，被城中部隊發覺執殺。
peopleEn: The first name written down for this war belongs to the Dingbian military governor Li Shiwang: in the tenth month of Xiantong, seeking credit for a frontier success, he killed the Nanzhao envoy Yang Qiaoqing and turned a quarrel that might have been settled into the reason for a war. The court then sent the deputy master of the Court of Public Works Dou Pang to replace him, and Dou Pang lost Qingxi Pass, lost Qianwei and lost Jiazhou in the space of a few weeks; in the fighting by the Dadu river he was so panic-stricken that he tried to hang himself with his own belt and had to be pulled down by the Xuzhou commander Miao Quanzhu, and he then fled alone on horseback to Daojiang, and was later demoted to a minor post at Kanzhou. The man who held his ground was the Dingbian army head An Zairong, who fell back to the north bank of the Dadu, shot at the enemy across the water and held out for nine days and eight nights; the Yuanhai commander Huang Zhuo was sent with five hundred men to check the advance at Muyuanchuan and was wiped out to the last man, with no word coming back. The pivot on the Chengdu side was the military governor Lu Dan, who hastily summoned the prefect of Pengzhou Wu Xinglu and the former prefect of Luzhou Yang Qingfu to repair the defences, posted notices to recruit braves, and enrolled three thousand of them as the Assault Corps. Yang Qingfu and the acting left deputy commander Li Xiang each led detachments of the Assault Corps out of the city, killing and wounding more than two thousand of the enemy and burning over three thousand of their siege engines, and Yang Qingfu then had melted iron poured down from the wall to beat back an enemy who had covered himself with a wet hide. The vanguard patrol officer Wang Zhou was sent to Hanzhou to ask for aid, the master of the imperial stables Zhi Xiang was appointed as the envoy for announcing and arranging peace, and Nanzhao sent its own officer Yang Dingbao to talk; the Right Wuwei general Song Wei arrived with two thousand men of the Zhongwu command, fought alongside the other armies, and drove Nanzhao back to the hill of Xingsu. There was treachery inside the walls as well: the officer Li Zixiao came to terms with Nanzhao in secret and prepared to burn the eastern granary as a signal, and he was found and put to death by the garrison.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬於極早的青銅冷兵器：銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上，造價低廉、重量輕、可以大量配發，埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。它並沒有出現在咸通十年的通鑑記載裡，此役留下的可核事實是另一套裝備。唐軍用弩、用弓：南詔與官軍隔大渡河「互相射擊」，夜襲時「亂發弓弩」，靠的就是大量攜帶的矢與輕便的弩機；攻城一方帶來雲梯與衝車，二月初一在成都四面架起，並拆下民間籬笆，浸濕彎曲以為篷，人藏其下舉而攻城，矢石不能入，火亦不能燒，這是守方最難對付的一種罩具。守方以火油澆燒、以熔化鐵汁澆灌，又令「突將」出城焚燒敵方攻具三千餘具。冷兵器方面，突將手中的長矛、大刀與百姓應召攜來的割草刀、木棒，同城頭的弓弩相配合；南詔主力為步騎，屢以乘船筏爭渡、搶奪渡口的辦法渡過大渡河，退走時又在雙流造橋突圍。運輸與後勤方面，唐軍靠漢州、導江、新津一線的集結與轉運，攻城器械、柴薪、矢石皆自城內調度，援軍則由興元、鳳翔兩路分道而來。戰後修築的壅門城、壕塹、分植的鹿角與營塞，則是城防器材的一次大規模補充；至於卡面這件兵器在其中的位置，只能說它與「突將」手中的長矛屬同一類型——以木杆配金屬矛頭、便於守城與出城反擊的廉價冷兵器。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on this card is a very early bronze cold weapon: a copper or bronze head bound onto a wooden shaft, cheap to make, light to carry, and issued in bulk; the Egyptians used it to hold city walls, and later to recover lost ground. It does not appear in the annals of the tenth year of Xiantong, and what the record of this war actually leaves us is a different set of equipment. The Tang troops used crossbows and bows: the Nanzhao and the imperial troops shot at each other across the Dadu river, and when they struck camp at night they let loose a wild volley of bows and crossbows, relying on the great number of arrows they carried and on crossbows light enough to move. The besiegers brought scaling ladders and battering rams, which they set up on all four sides of Chengdu on the first day of the second month, and they also broke down the fences of the countryside, soaked them and bent them into shields, and sheltered men underneath as they advanced on the wall, so that neither arrow nor stone could get in and fire could not take hold; this was the most awkward of all the cover for the defenders to answer. The defenders replied with burning oil, with melted iron poured down, and by sending the Assault Corps out of the city to burn more than three thousand of the enemy's siege engines. Among the cold weapons the spears and broadswords in the hands of the Assault Corps, together with the sickles and cudgels carried by the townspeople who came to help, worked together with the bows and crossbows on the wall. The Nanzhao main body was foot and horse; they repeatedly crossed the Dadu by pressing boat rafts and seizing the fords, and on the way out they built a bridge at Shuangliu to break through. As for transport and supply, the Tang army depended on assembly and transfer at Hanzhou, Daojiang and Xinjin, with siege engines, firewood and ammunition all drawn from inside the city, while the reinforcements came by two roads from Xingyuan and Fengxiang. The Yumen wall, the ditch, the planted deer-horn abatis and the stockades built after the war were a large-scale addition to the city's defensive materials; and as for the weapon on this card, its place can only be described as one of a kind: a cheap cold weapon of wood shaft and metal head, suited to holding a wall and to the sortie.
tactics: 南詔的戰術以欺騙與奇襲為主。十月先取歸附唐室的董春烏部，十一月進逼巂州；十二月中旬大軍分兵過雪嶺之坡，佔領沐源川，抄清溪關的側後；十四日更穿上被殲滅的兗海部隊軍裝，假扮敗兵在江邊喊船，待唐軍的船靠岸才暴露真容，隨即攻陷犍為。攻打嘉州時，又暗遣奇兵自東渡河，與正面之兵東西夾擊，殺忠武將顏慶師與嘉州刺史楊忞，逼得定邊監軍張允瓊奔潰。十二月二十九日大渡河邊一役，酋龍一面遣清平官假作講和，一面以船筏爭渡，忠武、徐宿兩軍列陣抗拒，官軍驚潰，竇滂被部將救下；諸將趁夜襲營，亂發弓弩，使南詔軍驚亂撤走。唐方的戰術則是先立城、後野戰。正月時成都無壕無備，盧耽以募兵補之，一邊遣使議和拖延以待援軍；南詔二十日抵城下，唐以子城固守，二十四日王晝在漢州南界毗橋與南詔先鋒接戰失利，退保漢州；竇滂因自己失地心態失衡，散布敵眾數十倍之說，使援軍逗留不進；城內又有人陰通南詔，約定焚燒東倉為內應，被發覺執殺；南詔攻城因無人內應而停。二月十一日顏慶復率軍進至成都府北四十五里的新都，十二日會戰大破，十三日再戰於沱江驛，十八日奪升遷橋，十九日追至雙流，攻城器械為官軍所焚。
tacticsEn: The Nanzhao tactic was built on deception and surprise. In the tenth month they first took the Dongchunwu tribe, which had submitted to the Tang, and in the eleventh month they pressed towards Xizhou. In the middle of the twelfth month the main body split off, crossed the slope of the Snow Ridge and occupied Muyuanchuan, getting in behind Qingxi Pass; on the fourteenth they put on the uniforms of the destroyed Yuanhai detachment, dressed as a beaten force and called out for the boats at the water's edge, and only exposed themselves once the Tang boats had come alongside, whereupon Qianwei fell. When they attacked Jiazhou they sent a column by night across the river to the east to fall on the defenders' flank while the main body engaged in front, killing the Zhongwu commander Yan Qingshi and the prefect of Jiazhou Yang Min and driving the Dingbian commissary Zhang Yunqiong into flight. In the action by the Dadu on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month the chieftain on the one hand sent his civil administrators forward to pretend to discuss terms, and on the other pushed boat rafts across to force a crossing, while the Zhongwu and Xusu commands drew up in array to meet them; the Tang line broke in panic, Dou Pang was pulled down by one of his own officers, and the generals then struck the Nanzhao camp at night, letting loose bows and crossbows at random so that the enemy broke up and withdrew. The Tang tactic was the opposite: first make the city stand, then fight in the open. In the first month Chengdu had no ditch and no defences, and Lu Dan repaired this by recruiting men, sending envoys to negotiate so as to gain time for the reinforcements, and holding the inner city while the enemy stood before it on the twentieth; on the twenty-fourth Wang Zhou met the Nanzhao vanguard at Pipi bridge on the southern edge of Hanzhou, was worsted, and fell back on Hanzhou. Dou Pang, burdened by the ground he had already lost, spread the report that the enemy was ten times their strength, and the reinforcements hung back and would not advance. Inside the city there was also a man in secret correspondence with Nanzhao who had undertaken to burn the eastern granary as a signal, and he was found and executed; the enemy halted its assault because no one answered from within. On the eleventh day of the second month Yan Qingfu led his army to Xindu, forty-five li north of the Chengdu prefectural seat, won a great victory there on the twelfth, fought again at the Tuojiang courier station on the thirteenth, took the Ascending-bridge on the eighteenth, pursued the enemy to Shuangliu on the nineteenth, and burned the siege engines.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時間：戰爭自咸通十年（八六九年）十月南詔攻破董春烏部起，至咸通十一年（八七〇年）二月南詔退走，歷時約五個月；記載最完整的戰鬥段落集中在咸通十年十二月十四日至次年二月十八日。兵力：南詔大軍為數萬之眾，二月十三日驃信又以步騎數萬增援；唐方常見的數字是突將三千人，援軍方面興元府六千人、鳳翔府四千人在漢州集結，竇滂自導江率四千人北上，毗橋一役王晝借得兵三千餘人。損失：黃卓部五百人全沒；十二月二十九日大渡河之役與嘉州之役，官軍散失甚眾；正月二十四日毗橋接戰失利退保漢州；二月十二日新都之戰，官方記南詔軍被殺二千餘人；二月十三日沱江驛會戰，記南詔死五千餘人，退保星宿山。攻城器械：二月初一之後官軍焚燒敵人攻具三千餘具。距離：新都在成都府治北四十五里，沱江驛在成都之北三十里。城池：事變之初成都只有子城，無壕無塹。相持：清溪關隔水相持九天八夜。參考文獻為《資治通鑑》卷二百五十一與卷二百五十二。各方確切的總傷亡、糧秣消耗與器械總數史無明文，只採可以互相印證的量級說法，不作精確斷言。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly these. Timing: the war runs from the tenth month of the tenth year of Xiantong, 869, when Nanzhao broke the Dongchunwu tribe, to the second month of the eleventh year, 870, when Nanzhao withdrew, a matter of about five months; the passages with the fullest detail run from the fourteenth day of the twelfth month of 869 to the eighteenth day of the second month of 870. Strength: the Nanzhao main army was some tens of thousands, and on the thirteenth day of the second month the chieftain brought up several tens of thousands of foot and horse in reinforcement; the figures usually given for the Tang side are three thousand men in the Assault Corps, with the reinforcements consisting of six thousand from Xingyuan Prefecture and four thousand from Fengxiang Prefecture assembled at Hanzhou, while Dou Pang led four thousand up from Daojiang, and at Pipi bridge Wang Zhou borrowed a little over three thousand men. Losses: the five hundred men of Huang Zhuo were destroyed to the last; at the action by the Dadu and at Jiazhou on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month the Tang troops were scattered heavily; on the twenty-fourth of the first month Wang Zhou was worsted at Pipi bridge and fell back on Hanzhou; at Xindu on the twelfth day of the second month the official record gives more than two thousand Nanzhao killed; at the action at the Tuojiang station on the thirteenth it gives more than five thousand Nanzhao dead and a retreat to the hill of Xingsu. Siege material: after the first day of the second month the Tang burned more than three thousand of the enemy's siege engines. Distances: Xindu lay forty-five li north of the Chengdu prefectural seat, and the Tuojiang station thirty li north of Chengdu. The city: at the outset of the affair Chengdu had only the inner city, with no ditch and no rampart. Duration of one stand: nine days and eight nights of shooting across the water at Qingxi Pass. The reference is the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, volumes 251 and 252. The exact total casualties on either side, the consumption of grain and fodder and the number of engines are not recorded; only the order of magnitude that can be cross-checked is given, and no exact assertion is made.
cause: 打起上來的直接導火線，是一樁外交事件被當權者用來換取邊功。咸通十年，定邊節度使李師望在與南詔往來之際殺死南詔使者楊酋慶，此舉本可引來跨境報復，卻正合李師望求取戰功以固位的目的。南詔驃信世隆隨即以董春烏部歸附朝廷為口實，點兵北上，戰端自十月開啟。朝廷換掉李師望，改派太府少卿竇滂接任，竇滂的處置又加速了局面惡化：他放棄外線城寨，把兵屯在大渡河一線，卻沒有加固沿線堡壘，黃卓部覆沒之後更未及時收束隊伍，使南詔得以利用缺口直入犍為、嘉州；清溪關失守後安再榮退保北岸，節制已無退路。深層的背景是唐西南邊防體系的空虛：成都在唐廷看來是業已安定的內府重鎮，年深日久只餘子城，壕塹既無、將士不習武備，節度使更替頻繁，遇警只能臨時募兵張榜。南詔則握有山谷行軍的優勢，往年攻蜀多取溪谷間道，秋冬水淺可涉大渡河，正合其季節性出兵的老規。於是一次大使被殺、一處邊部歸附，遇上守軍無備、統帥失方，就把整條川西南線拖進了戰爭。
causeEn: The direct spark was a diplomatic incident used by the man in office to buy himself credit on the frontier. In the tenth year of Xiantong the Dingbian military governor Li Shiwang killed the Nanzhao envoy Yang Qiaoqing during his dealings with the Nanzhao. The act could have brought a punitive raid across the border, and it suited Li Shiwang's purpose of winning a military distinction to strengthen his own position. The Nanzhao chieftain Shilang then took the submission of the Dongchunwu tribe to the Tang court as his pretext, called up his troops and marched north, and the war was open from the tenth month. The court replaced Li Shiwang and sent the deputy master of the Court of Public Works Dou Pang; his handling of the situation made matters worse again. He gave up the outlying forts and massed his troops on the line of the Dadu without strengthening the strongholds along it, and after the destruction of Huang Zhuo's five hundred men he did not rally his troops in time, so that Nanzhao could use the gap to drive straight into Qianwei and Jiazhou; after Qingxi Pass fell, An Zairong fell back on the north bank and the command had no road left. Behind all this lay the hollowness of the Tang defence in the south-west. To the court Chengdu was a settled inland prefecture, and in the course of years nothing remained but the inner city: there was no ditch, the soldiers no longer practised their arms, the governors changed hands often, and when the alarm came the only expedient was to post notices and recruit men in haste. Nanzhao, for its part, held the advantage of marching through mountain valleys, and in former years it had taken its roads into Sichuan along the streams and gorges, crossing the Dadu where the water was low in the autumn and winter, which fitted the old rhythm of its seasonal campaigning. So one murdered envoy and one submission on the frontier, met by a garrison without preparation and a commander who lost his head, dragged the whole south-western line of the river into war.
impact: 這一役對唐西南防務有兩重長遠影響。第一是制度層面：戰前成都其實沒有像樣的城防，只有一座子城，無壕無塹，士卒久不操演，兵源靠臨時張榜招募；戰後顏慶復主持修築壅門城，挖壕引水，分植鹿角，構建營塞，把成都從一座靠宮牆撐著的內府城市改成有雉堞、有壕溝、有鹿角障的邊防重鎮，成都的城防格局在此定型，其後百餘年仍以此為基礎增修。西南各州也在失守與收復之間加深了對渡口與隘路的依賴，興元、鳳翔方向的援軍路線與漢州、導江的集結點被固定下來，成為西川調度的常例。第二是人事與朝局：竇滂貶為康州司戶，顏慶復升任東川節度使並統一各軍調遣，戰後的職官調動把西川與東川的指揮權重新分合；宋威因爭功搶先入成都城下、意欲追擊，被顏慶復以牒文奪軍、勒令速回漢州，此事暴露了唐末援軍與節度使之間在指揮權與功名上的緊張，而募來的「突將」從此成為西川常備的突擊骨幹。南詔方面的影響則是反向的：此役之後南詔自知西川有備，而其內部變亂已起，進攻的意願與能力同時下降，成都與南詔之間的邊界在接下來的年月裡維持了一段相對安寧。
impactEn: This war had two long-term consequences for the south-western defence of the Tang. The first was institutional. Before the campaign Chengdu had no real defences at all: only the inner city, no ditch and no rampart, soldiers who had long ceased to drill, and troops obtained by posting notices and recruiting in haste. After the war Yan Qingfu had the Yumen wall built, with ditches drawing in water, deer-horn abatis planted and stockades raised, so that Chengdu changed from an inland prefecture resting on its palace walls into a frontier stronghold with parapets, a ditch and horned obstacles, and the layout of the city's defences was fixed at this point and was still built upon for more than a century afterwards. The other prefectures of the south-west, having been lost and retaken, grew correspondingly dependent on the fords and the passes, and the routes by which help came out of Xingyuan and Fengxiang, together with the assembly points at Hanzhou and Daojiang, were fixed into a regular practice of western-Sichuan dispatch. The second consequence lay in appointments and in the politics of the court: Dou Pang was demoted to a minor post at Kanzhou, Yan Qingfu was raised to be military governor of Dongchuan and given unified control of the relief armies, and the redistribution of offices after the campaign re-divided and re-joined the command between Xichuan and Dongchuan. Song Wei, having stolen ahead to the foot of Chengdu for the credit of the deed and wishing to pursue, was stripped of his command by a formal despatch from Yan Qingfu and ordered back to Hanzhou; the affair laid bare the strain between the arriving relief armies and the governors over command and over who took the credit. The men recruited as the Assault Corps from then on became the standing shock troops of western Sichuan. The effect on Nanzhao ran the other way: after this campaign the Nanzhao rulers knew that Xichuan was prepared, and with trouble already breaking out among themselves their will and their capacity to attack both fell away, and the frontier between Chengdu and Nanzhao enjoyed a period of relative quiet in the years that followed.
result: 結果是成都守住，南詔退兵。正月二十日南詔主力抵達成都城下，二月初一以雲梯、衝車四面猛攻，竇滂期援、盧耽無備，靠子城、新募突將與城頭火油勉力支撐；楊慶復與李驤出城反擊，殺傷二千餘人、焚燒攻具三千餘具，楊慶復又以熔化鐵汁澆退以濕篷蔽身之敵，攻城屢挫。二月初五酋龍請和，遣使迎接太僕卿支詳，然和議未定，南詔復攻城不輟；初九城中出兵抗擊，南詔始退，惟援軍先鋒顏慶復已率軍進至成都府北四十五里的新都，十二日大破南詔，殺二千餘人，百姓亦持割草刀與木棒相助；十三日右武衛上將軍宋威率忠武軍二千人與諸軍會戰於沱江驛，記南詔死五千餘人，退保星宿山；十八日唐軍奪升遷橋，南詔當夜自燒攻城具而走。追擊至雙流，南詔造橋逃竄，經邛州圍攻二日不克，遂退回本土。戰役之後，顏慶復主持築壅門城、開壕引水、分植鹿角、營建營塞，自此南詔知西川有備，其內亂又起，遂無力再寇成都；唐廷則以顏慶復為東川節度使、貶竇滂為康州司戶，收束了這場由一次外交殺人引發的戰事。
resultEn: The outcome was that Chengdu held and Nanzhao withdrew. The Nanzhao main body reached the foot of Chengdu on the twentieth day of the first month, and on the first day of the second month they attacked on all four sides with scaling ladders and battering rams. Dou Pang was waiting for relief and Lu Dan had no preparation, so the city stood on the inner walls, the newly recruited Assault Corps and the burning oil poured from the parapets. Yang Qingfu and Li Xiang went out of the city to counter-attack, killing and wounding more than two thousand and burning over three thousand of the enemy's engines, and Yang Qingfu then had melted iron poured down on the men who had covered themselves with wet hides; the assault was repelled again and again. On the fifth day of the second month the chieftain asked for peace and sent men to meet the envoy for peace, Zhi Xiang; but the terms were not settled and Nanzhao kept on assaulting. On the ninth the troops of the city sallied out and Nanzhao first drew off, though by then the leader of the relief force, Yan Qingfu, had already brought his army to Xindu, forty-five li north of the Chengdu prefectural seat, and on the twelfth he broke the Nanzhao army badly, killing more than two thousand, with the people of the district coming out with sickles and cudgels to help; on the thirteenth the Right Wuwei general Song Wei arrived with two thousand men of the Zhongwu command and fought the other armies in a pitched battle at the Tuojiang station, the record giving more than five thousand Nanzhao dead and a withdrawal to the hill of Xingsu; on the eighteenth the Tang army took the Ascending-bridge and that night the Nanzhao set their engines alight and ran. The pursuit went as far as Shuangliu, where the Nanzhao built a bridge and broke out, and after two fruitless days of besieging Qianzhou they withdrew to their own country. After the campaign Yan Qingfu had the Yumen wall built, the ditches opened and watered, the deer-horn abatis planted and the stockades raised; from that point the Nanzhao knew that Xichuan was prepared, trouble was already rising among themselves, and they had no strength left to attack Chengdu again. The court settled the matter by making Yan Qingfu military governor of Dongchuan and demoting Dou Pang to a minor post at Kanzhou, and so the war that had begun with a diplomatic killing was closed.
